Rare Chevy Camaro ZL1 Looks Like a GTA VI Prop, Yours If You Really Want It
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Chevrolet Camaro ZL1s are cool, but few are cooler than this example, which boasts numerous mods, has more power to play with, and is for sale in the United States of America.
Modded by Hendrick Motorsports and Callaway, it is called the Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 Coupe Hertz/Hendrick Motorsports Edition (Jeez, that’s a long name!), and you are looking at car #7 out of 24 built to this specification, as per the dashboard plaque. The muscle car in question is a 2020 model year, with 14,300 miles (23,000 km) under its belt, a clean California title, and a clean Carfax vehicle history report, meaning that it hasn’t been involved in any accidents, and has no mileage discrepancies.
The equipment list is extensive and comprises stuff such as the TripleCooled intercooler system and GenThree supercharger from Callaway, a set of 20-inch wheels finished in black with custom center caps, Hertz fender badges, Hertz yellow-finished brake calipers with the Hendrick Motorsports logo on them, a special build plaque with the VIN located under the hood, and oil filler cap, coolant reservoir cap, and brake reservoir cap with the #24 logo. The Hendrick Motorsports dashboard plaque with a signature and production number is also on deck.
Additional goodies of this 2020 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 Coupe Hertz/Hendrick Motorsports Edition include the Recaro Performance bucket seats for the driver and front passenger complete with embroidered headrests, embroidered floor and trunk mats, Hertz yellow-painted trim on the door cards, illuminated door sills that feature the Hertz logo on them, and a few other things. The listing also reveals the OEM hood insert with a cutout for the supercharger, a 1LE spoiler, and Diode Dynamics smoked side markers.
Photo: Cars&Bids As for the equipment installed at the factory during the muscle car’s production, it includes the head-up display, rear park assist, Magnetic Ride Control suspension, Brembo brakes, and limited-slip differential. Any muscle car enthusiast and their grandmother can tell you that this generation Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 came with a 6.2-liter supercharged V8, which pumped out 650 hp (485 kW/659 ps) and 650 pound-feet (881 Nm) of torque with no modifications whatsoever.
The stock vehicle required in the region of three and a half seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, and took a little over 11 seconds to run the standing quarter mile. However, due to some of the mods, this Chevy Camaro ZL1 is punchier. The engine is said to produce 750 hp (559 kW/760 ps) and 739 lb-ft (1,002 Nm) of torque, and it drives the rear wheels through a 10-speed automatic transmission. The performance hasn’t been mentioned in the ad, but we know that this model needed 3.2 seconds to hit the 60 mph mark.
Other than some chips on the front-facing surfaces, there are no other known issues, as this 2020 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 Coupe Hertz/Hendrick Motorsports Edition is in top-notch condition. The vehicle’s recent service history reveals that it had a four-wheel alignment performed in January 2023, September 2022, January 2022, and October 2022, at 7,145, 6815, 6,350, and 6,244 miles (11,499, 10,968, 10,219, 10,049 km), respectively. The engine oil and filter were changed in December and January 2024.
Photo: Cars&Bids Besides the muscle car, the next owner will get some service records, the owner’s manual, window sticker, a Hertz/Hendrick Motorsports build sheet, a Callaway Certificate of Authenticity and wall plaque, the Callaway carbon fiber engine cover signed by Reeves Callaway, a spare carbon fiber hood scoop, the OEM spoiler and sidemarkers, and one key.
The seller reportedly bought this modified and rare Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 in early 2023, adding some 6,600 miles (10,600 km) since, and he hasn’t revealed why he wants it gone. Interested parties should know that the title will only be available after the loan has been paid off, as there is a loan on this machine, and the sale proceeds will be used to satisfy it.
Given that the 2020 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 Coupe Hertz/Hendrick Motorsports Edition is a rare model, it is tricky to find out how much it is worth in today’s used car market in the United States of America. However, it appears that on average, this thing sells for approximately $90,000, and that’s more than the regular ZL1 version of the Chevy Camaro from the same model year, which fetches from $50,000 to over $80,000, depending on the usual factors.
As you can imagine, there is a reserve on it, and at $35,000, which was the highest bid at the time of writing, it obviously hasn’t been met. This modded ZL1 is going under the gavel as we speak on Cars&Bids, and the ongoing online auction will end on October 21, 2026. You can bid on it here , and before you click that link, feel free to tell us how much this machine is worth to you.
